entries.reason: Ability activations bind grant identity to ActionExecutionId; either destruction order must clear or stale-detect without retaining raw ActionExecution pointers.
evidence: docs/dev/战斗系统与动作编辑器.md
entries.create: AbilityRuntime::activate submits into the borrowed ActionRuntime and stores an owning AbilityActivation link with executionId.
entries.ownership: AbilityRuntime owns grant/activation records and step/cancel orchestration; ActionRuntime uniquely owns phase/execution state; the borrowed ActionRuntime must outlive AbilityRuntime. Script and combat façades project into AbilityRuntime rather than re-implementing advance-all loops.
entries.destroy_order: AbilityRuntime::cancel cancels through ActionRuntime then synchronizes; AbilityRuntime::step advances every active execution, cools down, then synchronizes (including after a partial advance failure); revoke rejects grants with active activations until synchronized/cancelled; ActionRuntime-first leaves synchronize detecting terminal or missing executions.
entries.restore: Process-local grant/activation identities are not a persistent wire format; restore rebuilds definitions then re-grants; in-flight activations are not reconstituted across process boundaries.
entries.stale: activate/findGrant/findDefinition/cancel/revoke/synchronize resolve by strong ids; missing grant/activation or terminal/missing execution returns structured NotFound rather than dangling pointers.

entries.reason: Ability definitions persist action timing, cooldown, instancing, activation group and gameplay-tag triggers in one schema shared by script and C++; timeline→definition assembly also lives on this asset face so script/combat do not duplicate split-timestamp timing rules.
evidence: docs/dev/战斗系统与动作编辑器.md
entries.schema: eve.action.ability Value document embedding ActionDefinition timing/timeline plus ability policy fields; abilityDefinitionFromTimeline assembles the same candidate from an ActionTimeline plus policy spellings.
entries.version: Current version 2 stores action phases and cooldown in nanoseconds.
entries.migration: Older ability documents migrate into a validated v2 candidate before publish; invalid identity or timing rejects the whole document.
entries.unknown_fields: Same-version unknown fields are ignored on read; encoders write the known v2 field set.
entries.restore_atomicity: decodeAbilityAsset and abilityDefinitionFromTimeline build a complete AbilityDefinition candidate and validate before the caller registers/replaces it in AbilityRuntime.

entries.reason: Runtime and editor share one versioned timeline asset; decode must not publish a partial candidate.
evidence: docs/dev/战斗系统与动作编辑器.md
entries.schema: eve.action.timeline Value document with tracks, Notify, NotifyState, metadata and payload extension slots.
entries.version: Current version 4; readers accept v1-v4 candidates and normalize writes to v4.
entries.migration: v1-v3 migrate into the v4 candidate (including Notify/NotifyState enabled defaulting to true); unknown higher versions are rejected before publish.
entries.unknown_fields: Same-version unknown fields are ignored on read; normalized save writes only known v4 fields.
entries.restore_atomicity: Decode constructs and fully validates a candidate ActionTimeline before replacing any published value; failure leaves prior state untouched.

entries.reason: Action is the L1 gameplay protocol host: ActionRuntime owns phase state; AbilityRuntime owns grants/cooldowns/step/cancel orchestration; AbilityAsset owns codec and timeline→definition assembly; EveScript and Combat only parse/project through façades.
evidence: docs/dev/战斗系统与动作编辑器.md
protocol: Native ActionRuntime/AbilityRuntime/AbilityAsset are the authoritative C++ faces; ScriptActionRuntime and ScriptCombatRuntime are façades that parse script scalars and project Result<Value> tables.

AbilityRuntime::step owns advance-all + cooldown + synchronize; abilityDefinitionFromTimeline owns timeline→definition assembly via actionTimingFromPhysicalSections; façades must not duplicate those loops.
ActionTiming is the sole ActionRuntime phase authority; timeline.duration must equal timing.total(); splitTimestamps are physical sections only (never read as phases).

Optional presentation/combat sinks (damage, audio, VFX, camera, state windows) are consumed through cap::forEach* inside ActionNotifyRegistry; absence is an observable NotFound path, not a silent success.

trim.absent_profile: Profiles without action drop the protocol host, script factory, and every dependent combat/RTS/tactics adapter that requires EVAction.

entries.thread_affinity: Owner/main composition thread for module construction, ScriptActionRuntime methods and ActionRuntime/AbilityRuntime advances; notify handlers run synchronously on the same owner thread and must not re-enter the block runtime.
cost_notes: AbilityRuntime::step is relative to active activation count; amortize per simulation step, not per grant.
